name: Alberto Tomba
milestone_by_age_26: Won two Olympic gold medals (giant slalom and slalom) at the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics at age 21, after securing his first World Cup victory in November 1987.
early_history_summary: Born to a wealthy Bolognese textile merchant, Tomba started skiing at age 7 under special teacher Roberto Siorpaes, a former national team skier, arranged by his father. He showed natural talent early, skied competitively through his teens, made his World Cup debut at 18 in 1985, and burst onto the scene with his first World Cup victory in November 1987 followed by double Olympic gold at Calgary in 1988.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and early intensive training
family_context_summary: Son of Franco Tomba, a wealthy Bolognese textile industry businessman who was a keen skier and arranged for special coaching from age 7. The family's wealth enabled access to training in Cortina d'Ampezzo and dedicated coaching.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Franco was a keen skier since attending college in Switzerland and procured a special teacher, Roberto Siorpaes, a former national team slalom skier, to train Alberto from age 7.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy family, dedicated coach from age 7, Cortina d'Ampezzo training, Italian skiing pipeline, early talent
evidence_summary: Tomba's path was shaped by his wealthy textile-merchant father who loved skiing and arranged for a former national team skier, Roberto Siorpaes, to coach Alberto from age 7. He trained intensively in Cortina d'Ampezzo, skied competitively from his early teens, and benefited from the Italian alpine skiing pipeline. His natural physical talent and power (182cm, 90kg) suited the new spring-loaded ski gates. By 21 he had won two Olympic golds, making him one of the greatest Alpine skiers in history.
starting_point: Born to a wealthy textile merchant family in Bologna, Italy; father Franco was a keen skier who arranged professional coaching from age 7.
current_position: Retired from competitive skiing in 1998 at age 31; lives in Castel de Britti, Italy; considered one of the greatest Alpine skiers in history with 3 Olympic golds, 2 World Championship golds, and 9 World Cup season titles.

name: Camilo Cienfuegos
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Battle of Yaguajay in December 1958 at age 26, a decisive guerrilla victory, and was appointed commander-in-chief of the Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces in January 1959.
early_history_summary: Born into a working-class Havana family of Spanish anarchist immigrants, Cienfuegos was politically active from his teens, attending art school before dropping out for financial reasons. He went to the US seeking work, returned to Cuba, joined anti-Batista protests, was shot in the leg in 1955, then went to Mexico and joined Castro's 26th of July Movement. He was one of 82 Granma expeditionaries in 1956 and rose rapidly to become a top guerrilla commander.
family_context_summary: Born into a working-class family in Havana; father Ramón was a tailor and Spanish anarchist involved in left-wing political activism. The family was politically engaged but financially modest.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a tailor and political activist involved with anarchist organizations (SIA, ALC), exposing Camilo to left-wing politics from childhood. Father took him to raise money for Spanish Republic orphans during the Civil War.
primary_early_advantage_tags: working-class, anarchist father, political repression, Castro network, guerrilla warfare, Che Guevara partnership
evidence_summary: Cienfuegos rose from a working-class Havana family of Spanish anarchist immigrants to become one of the top commanders of the Cuban Revolution by age 26. His father's political activism exposed him to left-wing ideas early, but his path was driven by adversity—poverty, political repression, being shot by Batista's soldiers—and by his embedding in Castro's revolutionary network alongside Che Guevara. His charisma and natural leadership made him a beloved figure among guerrillas and civilians. He won the decisive Battle of Yaguajay at 26 and was appointed commander-in-chief of the armed forces before his death at 27.
starting_point: Born into a working-class family in Havana, Cuba; father was a Spanish anarchist tailor who exposed him to left-wing politics from childhood.
current_position: Died on 28 October 1959 at age 27 when his plane disappeared over the Straits of Florida; final role: commander-in-chief of the Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces.

name: Shirin Ebadi
milestone_by_age_26: Became one of the first female judges in Iran in March 1969 at age 21-22, and earned a PhD with honors in private law from the University of Tehran in 1971 at age 23-24.
early_history_summary: Born in Hamadan to an academic family, Ebadi moved to Tehran as an infant. Her father was a law professor and chief notary public. She entered the University of Tehran Faculty of Law in 1965 at age 17-18, completed her law degree in three and a half years, passed the Department of Justice exams, and became a judge in March 1969. She continued her studies and earned her doctorate in 1971 while serving as a judge.
family_context_summary: Born into an educated Iranian family; father Mohammad Ali Ebadi was a law professor and chief notary public who wrote several books on commercial law. Mother was Minu Yamini. The family moved to Tehran when Shirin was one year old.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was one of the first lecturers in commercial law in Iran and wrote several books, providing direct domain expertise and academic modeling for Shirin's legal career.

evidence_summary: Ebadi's early trajectory was shaped by her father's legal expertise—he was one of Iran's first commercial law professors—and her admission to the University of Tehran at 17. She completed her law degree in just 3.5 years, became one of Iran's first female judges at 21-22, and earned a PhD at 23-24. The barriers she faced as a woman in Iran's legal system created urgency and distinction. Her Nobel Peace Prize (2003) came decades later, but her age-26 milestones were already exceptional: first female judge and PhD in law.
